result.title: FN-Prune: Training-Free Expert Pruning with Finite RMSNorm Perturbations
result.summary: Expert pruning reduces the memory footprint of mixture-of-experts language models, but retaining model quality depends on which experts are removed. Frequency- and magnitude-based scores measure the expert in isolation and overlook how normalization consumes its contribution: subtracting one expert changes both the direction of the residual stream and the scale applied to what remains. We propose FN-Prune, a training-free criterion that compares the next RMSNorm outputs before and after subtracting each router-weighted expert contribution, holding original routes and weights fixed. Squared differences are averaged over all calibration tokens in one pass; low-scoring experts are physically deleted at uniform per-layer ratios, and inference reroutes among survivors. At 50% expert removal, FN-Prune achieves lower WikiText-2 perplexity than the best published methods on Qwen3, ERNIE, and OLMoE, including a 32% reduction on OLMoE. At the same budget, GSM8K accuracy improves over the best published methods by 7.5 and 7.0 percentage points on Qwen3 and ERNIE, respectively, while multiple-choice gains remain task-dependent.

AI.brief_summary: FN-Prune 提出无需训练的 MoE 专家剪枝准则：固定原始路由与权重，比较减去单个加权专家贡献前后 RMSNorm 输出的平方差作为重要性分数，按每层统一比例删除低分专家，并在 Qwen3、ERNIE、OLMoE 上报告 50% 剪枝下的困惑度与 GSM8K 提升。
AI.relevance_reason: 其分数以「移除某专家后归一化输出如何变化」衡量真实贡献而非孤立权重，这种归一化敏感的扰动式归因，可能可供核查 latent 推理中按对后续状态影响归因模块／专家贡献与分配计算预算的做法。
